title.zh: 国际组织（豁免与特权）（国际刑事警察组织）命令 2012

completenessNote: 全文，共 11 条；逐字取自新加坡法规在线（SSO）官方打印视图，未改写、未节选。

text.en: 1. This Order is the International Organisations (Immunities and Privileges) (ICPO-INTERPOL) Order 2012.

3.—(1) ICPO‑INTERPOL is an organisation of which the Government and the governments of foreign sovereign Powers are members.
(2) ICPO‑INTERPOL has the legal capacities of a body corporate.

4.—(1) The premises of the Complex have the like inviolability as is accorded in respect of the official premises of an envoy of a foreign sovereign Power accredited to the Republic of Singapore, and no public officer or officer of a statutory body may enter those premises except with the consent of the Secretary General or the Executive Director of the Complex.
(2) The consent mentioned in sub‑paragraph (1) is implied in the case of fire or any other disaster requiring immediate action.
(3) ICPO‑INTERPOL must not permit the premises of the Complex to be used as a refuge for avoiding arrest under the laws of Singapore or in any other manner incompatible with its purposes.

heading.en: Immunities and privileges of delegates, observers, Executive Committee members, advisers and experts

text.en:
6.—(1) Each of the following persons, in the exercise of his or her functions and the accomplishment of his or her mission, while in Singapore and also (where applicable) during journeys made to or from the meeting place, enjoys the immunities and privileges set out in sub‑paragraph (2):
(a)delegates from foreign sovereign Powers which are members of ICPO‑INTERPOL, and observers attending conferences or meetings convened by ICPO‑INTERPOL;
(b)members of the Executive Committee;
(c)advisers and experts on mission to the Complex, and persons officially requested by ICPO‑INTERPOL to perform duties within the Complex.
(2) The immunities and privileges are —
(a)immunity from arrest and detention, except if caught in the act of committing an offence; and
(b)immunity from suit and legal process (even after completion of his or her mission) for acts performed in connection with his or her official duties and within the limits of his or her official capacity, provided that the immunity does not apply in the case of an offence against the written law relating to motor vehicle traffic committed by him or her, or of damage caused by a motor vehicle belonging to or driven by him or her.

heading.en: Immunities and privileges of Secretary General and directors of Complex
Immunities and privileges of Complex staff

text.en:
8.—(1) Every member of the staff of the Complex other than the Secretary General or a director of the Complex, who is duly accredited to the Government, enjoys the privileges and immunities set out in sub‑paragraph (2).
(2) The privileges and immunities mentioned in sub‑paragraph (1) are —
(a)immunity from suit and legal process (even after he or she has ceased to serve ICPO‑INTERPOL) in respect of all official acts performed by him or her in connection with his or her official duties and strictly within the limits of his or her official capacity; and
(b)exemption from taxation on his or her salary and emoluments paid to him or her by ICPO‑INTERPOL and derived from activities connected with the functions of the Complex.
(3) The immunity under sub‑paragraph (2)(a) does not apply in the case of an offence against the written law relating to motor vehicle traffic committed by him or her, or of damage caused by a motor vehicle belonging to or driven by him or her.

heading.en: Non-application of Part 4 of Second Schedule to Act

text.en: 9. Except as provided in paragraph 7(4), Part 4 of the Second Schedule to the Act does not apply to extend any immunity or privilege conferred by this Order to any person.

10.—(1) Any immunity or privilege under this Order (other than one enjoyed by the Secretary General) is to be waived by the Secretary General if it impedes the course of justice; but the waiver does not prejudice the interests of ICPO‑INTERPOL.
(2) Any immunity or privilege of the Secretary General under this Order may be waived by the Executive Committee.

11.—(1) Despite anything in this Order, no immunity or privilege under paragraph 6 or 7 may be enjoyed by any person who is a citizen or permanent resident of Singapore.
(2) Nothing in this Order affects the right of the Government to take any measure that it considers useful to safeguard national security, public safety or health, or to maintain law and order.
